main_body: Tall wooden medicine cabinet with a 3x4 grid of drawer or compartment fronts, a cream header band at the top and a dark red base
top_band: cream/tan band at rows 1-4 under a thin orange rim, with gold label marks on it, then dark red rows 5-6; it reads more like a header or cornice panel than a horizontal top
evidence: Down the middle column I see an orange rim, about 4 rows of cream carrying gold label marks, dark red rows 5-6, then the front face from row 7 to 27 made of repeated drawer fronts. There is no distinct lighter front-edge line between the cream band and the dark red. The gold marks on the cream suggest a vertical sign band, not a surface seen from above. The body is a flat straight-on grid of drawers with only a hat-like band on top, so it fails as a front elevation.

style.evidence: The outlines are dark red-brown and tinted, which is good. The wood has only about 4 tones (cream, tan, mid brown, dark red). The drawer fronts repeat identically and the frame is flat, with large areas of one brown and little grain or speckle. It is cleaner and thinner than the stall and well references, which carry more per-tile variation, so it falls short of the Beodeul bar.
